claim: Giardia lamblia has eight flagella organized as four bilaterally symmetric pairs.
source: Giardia has eight flagella organized as four bilaterally symmetric pairs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by the figures showing the flagellar organization.

claim: The eight flagella in Giardia have four different equilibrium lengths.
source: The eight flagella have four different equilibrium lengths, which implies a regulatory mechanism to sense and differentially modulate assembly or disassembly rates between the different flagellar pairs.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1.

claim: Each Giardia axoneme has a long cytoplasmic region extending from the basal body.
source: Each axoneme has a long cytoplasmic region extending from the basal body, and transitions to a canonical membrane-bound flagellum at the 'flagellar pore'.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Each flagellar pore is the site of IFT accumulation and injection.
source: We determined that each flagellar pore is the site of IFT accumulation and injection, defining a diffusion barrier functionally analogous to the transition zone.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by FRAP experiments and fluorescence intensity measurements in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: IFT-mediated assembly is length-independent in Giardia.
source: IFT-mediated assembly is length-independent, as train size, speed, and injection frequencies are similar for all flagella.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative measurements of IFT dynamics in Figure 4.

claim: Kinesin-13 localization to the flagellar tips is inversely correlated to flagellar length.
source: We demonstrate that kinesin-13 localization to the flagellar tips is inversely correlated to flagellar length.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 6.

claim: A length-dependent disassembly mechanism controls multiple flagellar lengths within the same Giardia cell.
source: Therefore, we propose a model where a length-dependent disassembly mechanism controls multiple flagellar lengths within the same cell.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by the experimental data and mathematical modeling throughout the manuscript.

claim: The anterior axonemes in Giardia have an average length of 19.1 ± 0.4 µm.
source: The anterior axonemes had an average length of 19.1 ± 0.4 µm, the caudal flagella were 20.5 ± 0.6 µm, the posteriolateral flagella were 16.2 ± 0.4 µm, and the ventral flagella were 16.8 ± 0.9 µm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The caudal flagella in Giardia have an average length of 20.5 ± 0.6 µm.
source: The anterior axonemes had an average length of 19.1 ± 0.4 µm, the caudal flagella were 20.5 ± 0.6 µm, the posteriolateral flagella were 16.2 ± 0.4 µm, and the ventral flagella were 16.8 ± 0.9 µm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The posteriolateral flagella in Giardia have an average length of 16.2 ± 0.4 µm.
source: The anterior axonemes had an average length of 19.1 ± 0.4 µm, the caudal flagella were 20.5 ± 0.6 µm, the posteriolateral flagella were 16.2 ± 0.4 µm, and the ventral flagella were 16.8 ± 0.9 µm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ventral flagella in Giardia have an average length of 16.8 ± 0.9 µm.
source: The anterior axonemes had an average length of 19.1 ± 0.4 µm, the caudal flagella were 20.5 ± 0.6 µm, the posteriolateral flagella were 16.2 ± 0.4 µm, and the ventral flagella were 16.8 ± 0.9 µm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The membrane-bound regions of anterior flagella in wild-type WBC6 trophozoites are 12.8 ± 0.1 µm.
source: We also confirmed the average lengths of membrane-bound regions in wild-type WBC6 trophozoites: anterior flagella were 12.8 ± 0.1 µm, caudal flagella were 8.1 ± 0.1 µm, posteriolateral flagella were 8.7 ± 0.2 µm, and ventral flagella were 13.7 ± 0.9 µm (Figure 1D and Hoeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1D, with citation to prior work.

claim: The membrane-bound regions of caudal flagella in wild-type WBC6 trophozoites are 8.1 ± 0.1 µm.

evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1D, with citation to prior work.

claim: The membrane-bound regions of posteriolateral flagella in wild-type WBC6 trophozoites are 8.7 ± 0.2 µm.
source: We also confirmed the average lengths of membrane-bound regions in wild-type WBC6 trophozoites: anterior flagella were 12.8 ± 0.1 µm, caudal flagella were 8.1 ± 0.1 µm, posteriolateral flagella were 8.7 ± 0.2 µm, and ventral flagella were 13.7 ± 0.9 µm (Figure 1D and Hoeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1D, with citation to prior work.

claim: The membrane-bound regions of ventral flagella in wild-type WBC6 trophozoites are 13.7 ± 0.9 µm.
source: We also confirmed the average lengths of membrane-bound regions in wild-type WBC6 trophozoites: anterior flagella were 12.8 ± 0.1 µm, caudal flagella were 8.1 ± 0.1 µm, posteriolateral flagella were 8.7 ± 0.2 µm, and ventral flagella were 13.7 ± 0.9 µm (Figure 1D and Hoeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 1D, with citation to prior work.

claim: All Giardia IFT-A homologs localize to the basal body region, flagellar pores, flagellar tips, and along the lengths of both cytoplasmic and membrane-bound regions of all axonemes.
source: All Giardia IFT-A (IFT121, IFT122, andIFT140) and IFT-B (IFT38, IFT54, IFT56, IFT57, IFT74/72, IFT80, IFT81, IFT88, and IFT172) homologs localized to the basal body region, flagellar pores, flagellar tips, and along the lengths of both the cytoplasmic and membrane-bound regions of all axonemes (Figure 2A and Hoeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A, with citation to prior work.

claim: All Giardia IFT-B homologs localize to the basal body region, flagellar pores, flagellar tips, and along the lengths of both cytoplasmic and membrane-bound regions of all axonemes.
source: All Giardia IFT-A (IFT121, IFT122, andIFT140) and IFT-B (IFT38, IFT54, IFT56, IFT57, IFT74/72, IFT80, IFT81, IFT88, and IFT172) homologs localized to the basal body region, flagellar pores, flagellar tips, and along the lengths of both the cytoplasmic and membrane-bound regions of all axonemes (Figure 2A and Hoeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A, with citation to prior work.

claim: Anterograde kinesin-2a and kinesin-2b motors localize to the eight flagellar pores and flagellar tips.
source: Anterograde kinesin-2a and kinesin-2b motors localized to the eight flagellar pores and flagellar tips, with less fluorescent signal on the cytoplasmic axonemes or basal bodies than tagged IFT proteins (Figure 2A and Hoeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A, with citation to prior work.

claim: BBS4 localizes primarily to the flagellar pores in Giardia.
source: Of the three BBSome homologs in Giardia, BBS4 localized primarily to the flagellar pores, BBS5 localized primarily to the cytoplasmic axonemes, and BBS2 localized primarily to the cytoplasm with some localization to the cytoplasmic axonemes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: BBS5 localizes primarily to the cytoplasmic axonemes in Giardia.
source: Of the three BBSome homologs in Giardia, BBS4 localized primarily to the flagellar pores, BBS5 localized primarily to the cytoplasmic axonemes, and BBS2 localized primarily to the cytoplasm with some localization to the cytoplasmic axonemes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: BBS2 localizes primarily to the cytoplasm with some localization to the cytoplasmic axonemes in Giardia.
source: Of the three BBSome homologs in Giardia, BBS4 localized primarily to the flagellar pores, BBS5 localized primarily to the cytoplasmic axonemes, and BBS2 localized primarily to the cytoplasm with some localization to the cytoplasmic axonemes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: IFT81mNG fluorescence is not uniformly distributed along the lengths of anterior or posteriolateral flagella.
source: IFT81mNG fluorescence was not uniformly distributed along the lengths of either the anterior or posteriolateral flagella (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The maximum fluorescence intensity of IFT81mNG for both anterior and posteriolateral flagella occurs at the flagellar pore.
source: The maximum fluorescence intensity for both flagella occurred at the flagellar pore, a region that lies at the transition from the cytoplasm to the compartmentalized flagellum (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: IFT proteins are dynamic at the flagellar pores.
source: IFT proteins are dynamic at the flagellar pores, as indicated by FRAP of the posteriolateral flagella in the IFT81mNG strain (Figure 3A, Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRAP experiments shown in Figure 3A and Video 1.

claim: IFT proteins are dynamic on cytoplasmic axonemes.
source: IFT proteins were dynamic on cytoplasmic axonemes, and recovery is likely bidirectional as the photobleached region did not change position during recovery.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRAP experiments shown in Figure 3B and Video 2.

claim: IFT turnover is approximately three times faster at the flagellar pore than in the cytoplasmic region.
source: IFT turnover was approximately three times faster at the flagellar pore (effective diffusion constant = 0.049 ± 0.017 µm2 s−1) than in the cytoplasmic region (effective diffusion constant = 0.018 ± 0.005 µm2 s−1) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The effective diffusion constant at the flagellar pore is 0.049 ± 0.017 µm2 s−1.
source: IFT turnover was approximately three times faster at the flagellar pore (effective diffusion constant = 0.049 ± 0.017 µm2 s−1) than in the cytoplasmic region (effective diffusion constant = 0.018 ± 0.005 µm2 s−1) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The effective diffusion constant in the cytoplasmic region is 0.018 ± 0.005 µm2 s−1.
source: IFT turnover was approximately three times faster at the flagellar pore (effective diffusion constant = 0.049 ± 0.017 µm2 s−1) than in the cytoplasmic region (effective diffusion constant = 0.018 ± 0.005 µm2 s−1) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The accumulation of IFT proteins at the flagellar pores is driven by diffusion of IFT proteins from the cytoplasmic axoneme region and the return of IFT trains undergoing retrograde transport.
source: We hypothesized that the different rates of IFT protein turnover between the cytoplasmic and flagellar pore regions are due to two processes that promote the accumulation of IFT proteins at the flagellar pore: (1) diffusion of IFT proteins from the cytoplasmic axoneme region and (2) the return of IFT trains undergoing retrograde transport (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 3F, supported by modeling and experimental data.

claim: The average anterograde IFT train speed for all flagellar pairs is between 3.0–3.2 µm/sec.
source: Specifically, the average anterograde IFT train speed for all flagellar pairs was between 3.0–3.2 µm/sec, with no significant differences between any of the measured flagella (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Retrograde IFT velocity is not significantly different from anterograde velocity in Giardia.
source: Retrograde IFT velocity was not significantly different from anterograde velocity and the average retrograde IFT velocity (~3.2 µm/sec) was not significantly different between any of the measured flagellar pairs (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claim: The average retrograde IFT velocity is approximately 3.2 µm/sec.
source: Retrograde IFT velocity was not significantly different from anterograde velocity and the average retrograde IFT velocity (~3.2 µm/sec) was not significantly different between any of the measured flagellar pairs (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claim: The average size of anterograde IFT trains in anterior flagella is 24% larger than those in the shorter caudal flagella.
source: The average size of anterograde IFT trains in anterior flagella was 24% larger than those in the shorter caudal flagella (Figure 4C), supporting a length-dependence of IFT train size for the anterior and caudal flagella.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: There are no significant differences between sizes of anterior and caudal retrograde IFT trains.
source: However, there were no significant differences between sizes of anterior and caudal retrograde IFT trains (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: There are no significant differences in IFT train size between anterior and posteriolateral flagella in either direction.
source: No significant differences in IFT train size were observed between anterior and posteriolateral flagella in either direction (Figure 4D,F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 4D and 4F.

claim: Anterograde IFT injection frequency is not significantly different between anterior, caudal, and posteriolateral flagella.
source: Comparisons of anterograde IFT injection frequency between anterior, caudal, and posteriolateral flagella showed that IFT train injection is not significantly different between flagella of different lengths (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: Retrograde IFT frequency is not significantly different between any of the flagella.
source: Retrograde IFT frequency was also not significantly different between any of the flagella (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claim: The distribution of time-lag between IFT train injections is exponential for the three pairs analyzed.
source: The distribution of time-lag between injections is exponential for the three pairs analyzed, indicating a single rate limiting step for IFT train injection in the anterograde direction (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The average time between IFT train injections is 1.0 ± 0.1 s for the anterior flagella.
source: The average time between IFT train injections was similar between the three flagellar pairs: 1.0 ± 0.1 s for the anterior flagella; 1.3 ± 0.2 s for caudal flagella; and 1.2 ± 0.1 s for posteriolateral flagella (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The average time between IFT train injections is 1.3 ± 0.2 s for caudal flagella.
source: The average time between IFT train injections was similar between the three flagellar pairs: 1.0 ± 0.1 s for the anterior flagella; 1.3 ± 0.2 s for caudal flagella; and 1.2 ± 0.1 s for posteriolateral flagella (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The average time between IFT train injections is 1.2 ± 0.1 s for posteriolateral flagella.
source: The average time between IFT train injections was similar between the three flagellar pairs: 1.0 ± 0.1 s for the anterior flagella; 1.3 ± 0.2 s for caudal flagella; and 1.2 ± 0.1 s for posteriolateral flagella (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: There is a strong linear relationship between the total integrated fluorescence intensity of IFT81GFP and equilibrium flagellar length (R2 = 0.89).
source: We observed a strong linear relationship between the total integrated fluorescence intensity and equilibrium flagellar length (R2 = 0.89) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The total amount of IFT trains within each Giardia flagellum scales linearly with length.
source: Thus, the total amount of IFT trains within each Giardia flagellum scales linearly with length, supporting a constant IFT injection rate for each flagellar type.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the data in Figure 5B.

claim: Following one-hour incubation with 20 µM Taxol, the anterior flagella increased in length by 19%.
source: Specifically, following one-hour incubation with 20 µM Taxol, the anterior flagella increased in length by 19%, the posteriolateral flagella by 27%, and the caudal flagella by 61% (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figures 5C and 5D.

claim: Following one-hour incubation with 20 µM Taxol, the posteriolateral flagella increased in length by 27%.
source: Specifically, following one-hour incubation with 20 µM Taxol, the anterior flagella increased in length by 19%, the posteriolateral flagella by 27%, and the caudal flagella by 61% (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figures 5C and 5D.

claim: Following one-hour incubation with 20 µM Taxol, the caudal flagella increased in length by 61%.
source: Specifically, following one-hour incubation with 20 µM Taxol, the anterior flagella increased in length by 19%, the posteriolateral flagella by 27%, and the caudal flagella by 61% (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figures 5C and 5D.

claim: The direct relationship between the total amount of IFT trains in each flagellum and its length is unchanged after Taxol treatment.
source: Despite flagellar length increases, the direct relationship between the total amount of IFT trains in each flagellum and its length was unchanged after Taxol treatment (Figure 5E), which is consistent with the length-independent injection of IFT trains.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: All flagellar pairs have steady-state length increases when kinesin-13 expression is inhibited by ~60%.
source: Here we extend prior work that characterized flagellar length defects in this strain (McInally et al., 2019) to show that all flagellar pairs have steady-state length increases when kinesin-13 expression is inhibited by ~60% (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 6A and 6B, with citation to prior work.

claim: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of anterior flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 1.1 ± 0.04 µm.
source: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of anterior flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 1.1 ± 0.04 µm, the posteriolateral by 0.9 ± 0.03 µm, the caudal by 3.1 ± 0.18 µm, and the ventral by 1.6 ± 0.06 µm (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of posteriolateral flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 0.9 ± 0.03 µm.
source: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of anterior flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 1.1 ± 0.04 µm, the posteriolateral by 0.9 ± 0.03 µm, the caudal by 3.1 ± 0.18 µm, and the ventral by 1.6 ± 0.06 µm (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of caudal flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 3.1 ± 0.18 µm.
source: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of anterior flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 1.1 ± 0.04 µm, the posteriolateral by 0.9 ± 0.03 µm, the caudal by 3.1 ± 0.18 µm, and the ventral by 1.6 ± 0.06 µm (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of ventral flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 1.6 ± 0.06 µm.
source: Compared to non-specific gRNA controls, the length of anterior flagella in the K13kd strain is increased by an average of 1.1 ± 0.04 µm, the posteriolateral by 0.9 ± 0.03 µm, the caudal by 3.1 ± 0.18 µm, and the ventral by 1.6 ± 0.06 µm (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Kinesin-13mNG localizes to all interphase microtubule structures, including the median body, the ventral disc, and distinct regions of all eight flagella.
source: Kinesin-13mNG localized to all interphase microtubule structures, including the median body, the ventral disc, and distinct regions of all eight flagella.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Kinesin-13mNG is distributed unevenly along all flagella, localizing primarily to the distal flagellar tips.
source: In contrast to the uniform kinesin-13mNG localization on the disc or median body, kinesin-13mNG was distributed unevenly along all flagella, localizing primarily to the distal flagellar tips, but also localizing to cytoplasmic axonemes and flagellar pores (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The maximum intensity of kinesin-13mNG fluorescence is at the distal region of the flagellar tips.
source: The maximum intensity of kinesin-13mNG fluorescence was at the distal region of the flagellar tips and intensity sharply decreased within the first micrometer from the tip (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Kinesin-13mNG fluorescence intensity is significantly greater at the tips of caudal flagella compared to the longer anterior flagella.
source: The quantification of kinesin-13mNG fluorescence intensity in the flagellar tip regions indicated significantly greater fluorescence intensity at the tips of caudal flagella compared to the longer anterior flagella (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The difference in kinesin-13mNG intensity between the posteriolateral flagella and anterior flagella is not statistically significant.
source: However, the difference in intensity between the posteriolateral flagella and anterior flagella is not statistically significant (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: After five hours of Taxol treatment the anterior flagella increased by 4.1 ± 0.2 µm.
source: After five hours of Taxol treatment the anterior flagella increased by 4.1 ± 0.2 µm, the posteriolateral increased by 4.3 ± 0.3 µm, the ventral increased by 4.5 ± 0.2 µm, and the caudal increased by 5.4 ± 0.4 µm (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: After five hours of Taxol treatment the posteriolateral flagella increased by 4.3 ± 0.3 µm.
source: After five hours of Taxol treatment the anterior flagella increased by 4.1 ± 0.2 µm, the posteriolateral increased by 4.3 ± 0.3 µm, the ventral increased by 4.5 ± 0.2 µm, and the caudal increased by 5.4 ± 0.4 µm (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: After five hours of Taxol treatment the ventral flagella increased by 4.5 ± 0.2 µm.
source: After five hours of Taxol treatment the anterior flagella increased by 4.1 ± 0.2 µm, the posteriolateral increased by 4.3 ± 0.3 µm, the ventral increased by 4.5 ± 0.2 µm, and the caudal increased by 5.4 ± 0.4 µm (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: After five hours of Taxol treatment the caudal flagella increased by 5.4 ± 0.4 µm.
source: After five hours of Taxol treatment the anterior flagella increased by 4.1 ± 0.2 µm, the posteriolateral increased by 4.3 ± 0.3 µm, the ventral increased by 4.5 ± 0.2 µm, and the caudal increased by 5.4 ± 0.4 µm (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the text and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: There are no significant differences in the elongation of the anterior, posteriolateral, or ventral flagella at the five-hour timepoint.
source: There were no significant differences in the elongation of the anterior, posteriolateral, or ventral flagella.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The caudal flagella increased by a significantly greater amount than the other three pairs of flagella at the five-hour time point.
source: However, the caudal flagella increased by a significantly greater amount than the other three pairs of flagella at the five-hour time point.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The fluorescence intensity at the distal flagellar tips decreased slightly with Taxol-induced flagellar elongation in all measured flagella, but these differences are not statistically significant.
source: The fluorescence intensity at the distal flagellar tips decreased slightly with Taxol-induced flagellar elongation in all measured flagella, but these differences are not statistically significant (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The rate of exponential decay of kinesin-13mNG with distance from the distal flagellar tip is unchanged in Taxol-elongated flagella.
source: Consistent with length-independent decay, the rate of exponential decay of kinesin-13mNG with distance from the distal flagellar tip was unchanged in Taxol-elongated flagella (Figure 8E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 8E and 8F.

claim: The maximum fluorescence recovery for all flagella is approximately 30% of the initial fluorescence intensity, representing a small mobile fraction of kinesin-13 in all flagella.
source: The maximum fluorescence recovery for all flagella was approximately 30% of the initial fluorescence intensity, representing a small mobile fraction of kinesin-13 in all flagella (Figure 8H, Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8H and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Giardia lacks a transition zone or TZ protein homologs.
source: Giardia flagella lack a transition zone or TZ protein homologs, yet the genome encodes homologs of IFT train components (IFT-A and IFT-B proteins), kinesin-2 and IFT dynein motors (Avidor-Reiss and Leroux, 2015; Barker et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The Giardia genome encodes homologs of IFT train components (IFT-A and IFT-B proteins), kinesin-2 and IFT dynein motors.
source: Giardia flagella lack a transition zone or TZ protein homologs, yet the genome encodes homologs of IFT train components (IFT-A and IFT-B proteins), kinesin-2 and IFT dynein motors (Avidor-Reiss and Leroux, 2015; Barker et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Kinesin-2 and kinesin-13 regulate flagellar assembly and disassembly in Giardia.
source: Similar to other eukaryotes, kinesin-2 and kinesin-13 regulate flagellar assembly and disassembly in Giardia, as CRISPRi-based knockdowns or the overexpression of dominant negatives result in dramatic flagellar length defects (Dawson et al., 2007; McInally et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: During Giardia cell division, four intact mature axonemes and basal bodies are structurally inherited (anterior and caudal) and four new axonemes are assembled de novo in each daughter cell.
source: Lastly, during cell division, four intact mature axonemes and basal bodies are structurally inherited (anterior and caudal) and four new axonemes are assembled de novo in each daughter cell (Hardin et al., 2017; Nohynková et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The cytoplasmic regions of the de novo posteriolateral and ventral axonemes are assembled prior to cytokinesis.
source: The cytoplasmic regions of the de novo posteriolateral and ventral axonemes are assembled prior to cytokinesis (Hardin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Equilibrium axoneme lengths of all eight flagella in Giardia are sensitive to MT stabilizing or depolymerizing drugs.
source: Equilibrium axoneme lengths of all eight flagella are also sensitive to MT stabilizing or depolymerizing drugs (Dawson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Each of the eight Giardia axonemes retains the characteristic '9+2' MT architecture.
source: While each of the eight axonemes retains the characteristic '9+2' MT architecture, each axoneme also has a cytoplasmic, non-membrane-bound region that extends from a centrally located basal body before exiting the cell body as a membrane-bound flagellum (McInally and Dawson, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Each Giardia axoneme has a cytoplasmic, non-membrane-bound region that extends from a centrally located basal body before exiting the cell body as a membrane-bound flagellum.
source: While each of the eight axonemes retains the characteristic '9+2' MT architecture, each axoneme also has a cytoplasmic, non-membrane-bound region that extends from a centrally located basal body before exiting the cell body as a membrane-bound flagellum (McInally and Dawson, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: The eight flagellar pore complexes are functionally analogous to the transition zone.
source: Thus, we contend that the eight flagellar pore complexes are functionally analogous to the transition zone, concentrating IFT proteins and acting as a diffusion barrier between the cytoplasmic and membrane-bound axoneme compartment.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the experimental data.

claim: The flagellar pores are the sites of IFT injection into the membrane-bound axonemes.
source: Furthermore, this work supports that the flagellar pores are the sites of IFT injection into the membrane-bound axonemes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the experimental data.

claim: Immature IFT particles first associate with cytoplasmic axonemal regions and mature at the eight flagellar pores, prior to their injection into the compartmentalized, membrane-bound axonemal region.
source: Though we currently lack direct spatial resolution of IFT particle maturation in Giardia, we speculate that immature IFT particles first associate with cytoplasmic axonemal regions and mature at the eight flagellar pores, prior to their injection into the compartmentalized, membrane-bound axonemal region.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation in the text.

claim: Kinesin-13 is a cargo of IFT in Giardia.
source: In the absence of other active transport mechanisms within the membrane-bound flagellum, we propose that kinesin-13 is a cargo of IFT (Piao et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Kinesin-13 mediated disassembly activity at the distal tips is a primary driver of differential flagellar length regulation in Giardia.
source: Due to turnover of kinesin-13 at the distal flagellar tip, coupled with the apparent exponential distribution of kinesin-13 fluorescence intensity within the flagellum (Figure 8), we suggest that the kinesin-13 mediated disassembly activity at the distal tips is a primary driver of differential flagellar length regulation in Giardia.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Giardia controls flagellar length through the modulation of axonemal-specific, length-dependent flagellar disassembly rates.
source: We propose a model where Giardia controls flagellar length through the modulation of axonemal-specific, length-dependent flagellar disassembly rates, rather than length-dependent IFT-mediated assembly rates as reported in other systems.
evidence: This is the main model proposed in the text based on the experimental findings.

claim: During flagellar assembly, kinesin-13 is transported to the flagellar tips from a flagellum-specific reservoir via anterograde IFT.
source: We propose that during flagellar assembly, kinesin-13 is transported to the flagellar tips from a flagellum-specific reservoir (possibly the flagellar pores) via anterograde IFT (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 7C.

claim: As the flagellum elongates, kinesin-13 is depleted from the reservoir while accumulating at the tip.
source: As the flagellum elongates, kinesin-13 is depleted from this reservoir while accumulating at the tip (Figure 7A inset).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 7A.

claim: The concentration of kinesin-13 at the distal tip increases until it reaches the critical concentration at which point the kinesin-13-mediated disassembly balances the assembly rate.
source: The concentration of kinesin-13 at the distal tip increases until it reaches the critical concentration at which point the kinesin-13-mediated disassembly balances the assembly rate (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 7B.

claim: Kinesin-13 does not undergo directed retrograde transport on the axoneme, but rather diffuses from the flagella tip toward the base.
source: The sharp decrease in fluorescence intensity immediately proximal to the flagellar tip suggests that kinesin-13 does not undergo directed retrograde transport on the axoneme, but rather diffuses from the flagella tip toward the base (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 7C, based on the fluorescence data.

claim: During diffusion from the flagellar tip, kinesin-13 is recaptured by anterograde IFT trains, sequestering it to the tip region.
source: Furthermore, this exponential decay suggests that during diffusion from the flagellar tip, kinesin-13 is recaptured by anterograde IFT trains, sequestering it to the tip region (Naoz et al., 2008) (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work and illustrated in Figure 7C.

claim: IFT81mNG is at least 3-fold brighter than IFT81GFP.
source: IFT81mNG was at least 3-fold brighter than IFT81GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The majority of kinesin-13 is localized to the flagellar tip at equilibrium, with minimal fluorescence intensity measured along the length of the membrane-bound axoneme.
source: We also found that the majority of kinesin-13 is localized to the flagellar tip at equilibrium, with minimal fluorescence intensity measured along the length of the membrane-bound axoneme (Figure 6D, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6D and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The initial rates of recovery of kinesin-13 fluorescence are similar at the tips of all types of flagella analyzed.
source: The initial rates of recovery of kinesin-13 fluorescence were similar at the tips of all types of flagella analyzed (Figure 8G and H, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 8G, 8H, and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Giardia has 198 Nek proteins whose functions are yet to be determined.
source: Several kinases are known to regulate either assembly or disassembly rates in Tetrahymena and Chlamydomonas (CALK, LF4, Nrks/Neks), and Giardia has 198 Nek proteins whose functions are yet to be determined (Berman et al., 2003; Bradley and Quarmby, 2005; Hilton et al., 2013; Manning et al., 2011; Meng and Pan, 2016; Wloga et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Kinesin-13 activity may indirectly impact IFT-mediated assembly by modulating cytoplasmic tubulin pools.
source: In addition to a direct role in MT disassembly at the flagellar tips, it is possible that kinesin-13 activity indirectly affects IFT-mediated assembly by regulating cytoplasmic tubulin pools through liberation of tubulin subunits from the median body (Dawson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a possibility in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: The median body has been proposed to act as a cytoplasmic reservoir of tubulin prior to cell division.
source: The median body (Figure 1, 'MB') is a semi-organized interphase MT array that has been proposed to act as a cytoplasmic reservoir of tubulin prior to cell division (Hardin et al., 2017) and overexpression of a rigor mutant kinesin-13 affected median body volume as well as flagellar lengths (Dawson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Overexpression of a rigor mutant kinesin-13 affected median body volume as well as flagellar lengths.
source: The median body (Figure 1, 'MB') is a semi-organized interphase MT array that has been proposed to act as a cytoplasmic reservoir of tubulin prior to cell division (Hardin et al., 2017) and overexpression of a rigor mutant kinesin-13 affected median body volume as well as flagellar lengths (Dawson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Neither kinesin-2 knockdown nor the expression of a dominant negative kinesin-2 affect cytoplasmic axoneme length.
source: Neither kinesin-2 knockdown nor the expression of a dominant negative kinesin-2 affect cytoplasmic axoneme length (Hoeng et al., 2008; McInally et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The lack of active transport of IFT proteins on cytoplasmic regions supports an IFT-independent mechanism for the de novo assembly of the posteriolateral and ventral flagellar pairs.
source: While we have not directly imaged the assembly of the cytoplasmic axonemal regions in this study, the lack of active transport of IFT proteins on cytoplasmic regions supports an IFT-independent mechanism for the de novo assembly of the posteriolateral and ventral flagellar pairs (Hardin et al., 2017; Sagolla et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Membrane-bound regions of flagella are assembled using IFT-mediated mechanisms.
source: While membrane-bound regions are assembled using IFT-mediated mechanisms (Hoeng et al., 2008; McInally et al., 2019), the cytoplasmic regions of each axoneme may be assembled in an IFT-independent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The cytoplasmic regions of each Giardia axoneme may be assembled in an IFT-independent manner.
source: While membrane-bound regions are assembled using IFT-mediated mechanisms (Hoeng et al., 2008; McInally et al., 2019), the cytoplasmic regions of each axoneme may be assembled in an IFT-independent manner.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility in the text.

claim: The apicomplexans Plasmodium and Toxoplasma lack IFT, BBsome, or TZ components and use IFT-independent or compartment-independent mechanisms to assemble flagella.
source: Atypical modes of ciliogenesis are not unprecedented, as the apicomplexans Plasmodium and Toxoplasma also lack IFT, BBsome, or TZ components and use IFT-independent or compartment-independent mechanisms to assemble flagella with no membrane invagination or basal body migration (Avidor-Reiss and Leroux, 2015; Barker et al., 2014; Briggs et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Both mammalian and Drosophila sperm flagella employ variations of cytoplasmic ciliogenesis that require the invagination of the basal body into the cytoplasm following the initiation of compartmentalized ciliogenesis.
source: Both mammalian and Drosophila sperm flagella also employ variations of cytoplasmic ciliogenesis that require the invagination of the basal body into the cytoplasm following the initiation of compartmentalized ciliogenesis (Avidor-Reiss et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: The 'balance-point model' argues that constitutively controlled steady-state flagellar length is a balance between a length-dependent assembly rate and a length-independent disassembly rate.
source: Built on this and other prior work, the prevailing explanation for the regulation of equilibrium flagellar length is the 'balance-point model', which argues that constitutively controlled steady-state length is a balance between a length-dependent assembly rate and a length-independent disassembly rate (Marshall et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Equilibrium flagellar length can be altered by modulating either the rates of flagellar assembly or disassembly.
source: However, equilibrium length can be altered by modulating either the rates of flagellar assembly or disassembly (Mohapatra et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: IFT-mediated assembly has been presumed to be the primary driver of ciliary length.
source: While IFT-mediated assembly has been presumed to be the primary driver of ciliary length (Engel et al., 2009; Hendel et al., 2018; Ludington et al., 2015), flagellar disassembly can also modify flagellar equilibrium length as defined by the balance point model.
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Kinesin-13 was first identified as a depolymerizer of cytoplasmic and spindle MTs.
source: Kinesin-13 (and kinesin-8) were first identified as depolymerizers of cytoplasmic and spindle MTs, but later were discovered to depolymerize MTs at distal ciliary tips (Helenius et al., 2006; Walczak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Kinesin-13 was later discovered to depolymerize MTs at distal ciliary tips.
source: Kinesin-13 (and kinesin-8) were first identified as depolymerizers of cytoplasmic and spindle MTs, but later were discovered to depolymerize MTs at distal ciliary tips (Helenius et al., 2006; Walczak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: In Giardia and in other microbial flagellates like Leishmania, kinesin-13 activity at the ciliary tips directly contributes to flagellar disassembly.
source: In Giardia (Dawson et al., 2007) and in other microbial flagellates like Leishmania, kinesin-13 activity at the ciliary tips directly contributes to flagellar disassembly, yet may also indirectly impact IFT-mediated assembly by modulating cytoplasmic tubulin pools (Blaineau et al., 2007; Chan and Ersfeld, 2010; Piao et al., 2009; Vasudevan et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: In Chlamydomonas, kinesin-13 promotes disassembly of axonemes via IFT transport during the induction of flagellar resorption.
source: In Chlamydomonas, kinesin-13 promotes disassembly of axonemes via IFT transport during the induction of flagellar resorption. Depletion of kinesin-13 prevents depolymerization of cortical MTs resulting in shorter flagella due to the reduction of the cytoplasmic tubulin pool required for IFT-mediated assembly (Piao et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Depletion of kinesin-13 in Chlamydomonas prevents depolymerization of cortical MTs resulting in shorter flagella due to the reduction of the cytoplasmic tubulin pool required for IFT-mediated assembly.
source: In Chlamydomonas, kinesin-13 promotes disassembly of axonemes via IFT transport during the induction of flagellar resorption. Depletion of kinesin-13 prevents depolymerization of cortical MTs resulting in shorter flagella due to the reduction of the cytoplasmic tubulin pool required for IFT-mediated assembly (Piao et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Over 500 distinct proteins comprise the highly conserved axoneme architecture.
source: Over 500 distinct proteins comprise the highly conserved axoneme architecture, defined by nine MT doublets surrounding a central MT pair ('9+2') (Ishikawa, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Axonemes are nucleated at basal bodies and extend from the complex transition zone.
source: Axonemes are nucleated at basal bodies and extend from the complex transition zone (TZ), which acts as a diffusion barrier at the base of the membrane-bound cilium (Reiter et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: The transition zone acts as a diffusion barrier at the base of the membrane-bound cilium.
source: Axonemes are nucleated at basal bodies and extend from the complex transition zone (TZ), which acts as a diffusion barrier at the base of the membrane-bound cilium (Reiter et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Assembly and maintenance of flagellar length is dependent upon bidirectional MT motor-driven intraflagellar transport (IFT) to provide building blocks to the site of assembly, the distal flagellar tip.
source: Assembly and maintenance of flagellar length is dependent upon bidirectional MT motor-driven intraflagellar transport (IFT) to provide building blocks to the site of assembly, the distal flagellar tip (Kozminski et al., 1993; Marshall and Rosenbaum, 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Canonical axoneme architecture, as well as IFT components and flagellar assembly mechanisms, likely predate the radiation of all extant lineages.
source: Canonical axoneme architecture, as well as IFT components and flagellar assembly mechanisms, likely predate the radiation of all extant lineages (Ishikawa, 2017; Sung and Leroux, 2013) due to widespread conservation in diverse unicellular flagellates ranging from Chlamydomonas, Tetrahymena, and Trypanosoma to the ciliated cell types of invertebrates and mammals (Buisson et al., 2013; Hao and Scholey, 2009; Kozminski et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The 'long-zero' experiment in Chlamydomonas demonstrated length equalization of both flagella when one was amputated, implying that a limited precursor pool is shared between flagella.
source: The classic 'long-zero' experiment in Chlamydomonas demonstrated length equalization of both flagella when one was amputated, and thus implies that a limited precursor pool is shared between flagella (Coyne and Rosenbaum, 1970).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: In Chlamydomonas, IFT train injection decreases with increasing flagellar length to provide a length-dependent assembly rate.
source: The length-independent IFT injection observed in Giardia contrasts with observations in the green alga Chlamydomonas, where IFT train injection decreases with increasing flagellar length to provide a length-dependent assembly rate (Chien et al., 2017; Hendel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Length-independent injection of IFT trains has recently been observed in Trypanosoma.
source: Length-independent injection of IFT trains has recently been observed in Trypanosoma and a 'grow-and-lock' model has been proposed wherein the flagellum grows at a constant rate until it is locked into a stable length (Bertiaux et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: A 'grow-and-lock' model has been proposed for Trypanosoma wherein the flagellum grows at a constant rate until it is locked into a stable length.
source: Length-independent injection of IFT trains has recently been observed in Trypanosoma and a 'grow-and-lock' model has been proposed wherein the flagellum grows at a constant rate until it is locked into a stable length (Bertiaux et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: In Leishmania, overexpression of one kinesin-13 homolog promotes decreased flagellar length.
source: In Leishmania, overexpression of one (of the five) kinesin-13 homologs promotes decreased flagellar length, whereas the knockdown of the orthologous kinesin-13 in Trypanosoma brucei promotes increased flagellar length (Blaineau et al., 2007; Chan and Ersfeld, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The knockdown of kinesin-13 in Trypanosoma brucei promotes increased flagellar length.
source: In Leishmania, overexpression of one (of the five) kinesin-13 homologs promotes decreased flagellar length, whereas the knockdown of the orthologous kinesin-13 in Trypanosoma brucei promotes increased flagellar length (Blaineau et al., 2007; Chan and Ersfeld, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: In Tetrahymena, cell body MTs are shortened by kinesin-13, but this activity is not required for liberating ciliary precursor tubulin.
source: Lastly, in Tetrahymena, cell body MTs are shortened by kinesin-13, but this activity is not required for liberating ciliary precursor tubulin.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: Kinesin-13 generally depolymerizes the ends of microtubules via ATP hydrolysis and undergoes one dimensional diffusion along the lattice with no preference for either the plus or minus-end of the microtubule.
source: Generally, kinesin-13 depolymerizes the ends of microtubules via ATP hydrolysis and undergoes one dimensional diffusion along the lattice with no preference for either the plus or minus-end of the microtubule (Cooper and Schafer, 2000; Desai et al., 1999; Hunter et al., 2003; Helenius et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.
